bug_semantics: The volume-target PATCH handler authorized baremetal:volume:update, loaded the complete existing VolumeTarget, applied even an unrelated permitted patch such as one to extra, persisted it, and serialized the returned object with convert_with_links without either enforcing baremetal:volume:view_target_properties on the response or masking password-like values in properties. A project-scoped caller allowed to update a target but forbidden to view target properties could therefore use the 200 PATCH response to read pre-existing iSCSI credentials. POST also returned properties unredacted, but those values had just been supplied by that caller and are not the confidentiality escalation at the root of this CVE.
flaw_origin: The response-sanitization omission was introduced with the original volume-target REST API in c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d (released in 9.0.0). It became a privilege-boundary vulnerability when project-scoped volume target access was added in e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9, which is contained in 17.0.0 but no 16.* tag. Later commit 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 only converted the endpoint representation and preserved the same unsanitized PATCH response, so it is a refactor rather than the BIC.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object has no AI author/co-author/Generated-with marker; see evidence
evidence: First-party OSSA-2026-023 (https://security.openstack.org/ossa/OSSA-2026-023.html) describes valid POST/PATCH access to /v1/volume/targets returning sensitive properties such as iSCSI credentials; its note says the code path existed since 9.0.0 but became a privilege escalation after 17.0.0 with project-scoped owner/lessee access. It declares affected ranges >=17.0.0 <29.0.6, >=30.0.0 <32.0.2, >=33.0.0 <35.0.2, and >=36.0.0 <37.0.1, and links the master and stable fixes.

In the read-only clone, `git log 00eda8b9c6391574ec8226a8c560aa51651d2019 -L 323,407:ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` follows the PATCH function back to c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d, where the new file first loaded the whole target, applied a patch, updated it, then executed `api_target = VolumeTarget.convert_with_links(new_target)` and returned it without redaction. The history also shows 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 merely changing the representation while preserving that behavior.

The independent pickaxe `git log --all -S'api_target = VolumeTarget.convert_with_links(new_target)' -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` returns only c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d (addition) and 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 (representation rewrite), corroborating c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d as the smallest public-history origin rather than the later refactor.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only ddcd97714cd5b27ac43ac0ef1138c13392223b90 -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_connector.py` produces no output, while `git show c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` shows the file as `new file mode 100644` with the vulnerable POST/PATCH implementations. Thus the vulnerable lines are absent from the immediate parent.

Release-boundary checks: `git tag --contains c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d --list '9.0.0'` returns 9.0.0 and the corresponding '8.*' query returns nothing. `git tag --contains e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 --list '17.*'` includes 17.0.0 while the '16.*' query returns nothing. For a released stable boundary present in the clone, direct backport 49bff4c09acfdf195f40f911236b9ac5c6def3c5 is contained in 29.0.6 and in no earlier 29.0.* tag. The remaining first-patched versions are those declared by OSSA/GHSA; their direct backports are present on the corresponding remote stable branches even where this frozen clone has no resulting release tag.

Fix verification: parent 00eda8b9c6391574ec8226a8c560aa51651d2019 has view_target_properties checks on read paths but PATCH line 404 directly converts new_target and has neither target_sanitize nor mask_dict_password. `git show dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd -- ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py` adds target_sanitize using strutils.mask_dict_password for all serialized properties and adds a PATCH-time baremetal:volume:view_target_properties check that invokes _redact_target_properties before conversion. The advisory directly references dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are identical.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d` shows author Satoru Moriya, committer Hironori Shiina, three named human Co-Authored-By trailers (Tomoki Sekiyama, David Lenwell, Hironori Shiina), Change-Id and Partial-Bug trailers, and no bot identity, AI co-author, Assisted-By, Generated-with, or other AI marker. No later commit's marker is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The original 2017 volume-target API commit is the causal code origin because it first created the PATCH response path that serialized the full updated object without secrecy enforcement; its parent has no volume-target API file. Line history and pickaxe both distinguish that origin from the 2020 plain-JSON refactor. Project-scoped RBAC later made the omission exploitable across a real privilege boundary, but it did not write the unsafe response behavior and therefore does not replace the smallest BIC. The direct security fix closes both layers by enforcing the view-properties policy on PATCH and by masking password-like fields during all target serialization. The BIC commit object contains only human identities and ordinary Gerrit/bug trailers, with no AI signal, so the protocol requires NOT_AI even though AI may have participated in discovery or a later fix.
